To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

treatment with interleukin-1 beta (IL-1 beta), interleukin-6 (IL-6), or interleukin (IL-8) alone, or IL-8 with interleukin (10) (IL-10) significantly inhibited the growth of human breast carcinoma xenografts in athymic mice.
the combined administration of IL- 2 with IFN-gamma significantly enhanced the therapeutic activity of DOX against a transplantable colo-rectal tumour in the rat.
the combination of IL-2 and IFN-gamma significantly enhanced the antitumoral activity of DOX in a rat model of colon carcinoma, without increasing the toxicity of DOX.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the treatment of cancer, based on the combination of conventional chemotherapy with biological response modifiers (BRMs), in the form of cytokines.
the development of a new therapeutic modality which combines the use of conventional chemotherapy with cytokines.
the development of a novel therapeutic regimen which combines a chemotherapeutic agent, doxorubicin, with the cytokines, interferon-gamma or interleukin 2, to enhance its efficacy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of DOX, IFN-g and IL-2 was superior to any of the single agents or combinations tested in this study.

the administration of IL-1 and IL-6 in the presence of IL-2 and IFN-gamma significantly enhances the therapeutic efficacy of DOX without any increase in the acute toxicity of the chemotherapeutic agent.

IFN-gamma, IL-2, and DOX, when administered in combination, are significantly more effective in inhibiting tumour growth in the rat colon carcinoma model than any of the three drugs administered alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of DOX with IFN-gamma or IL-2 is more effective than either cytokine or drug given alone and that the combination of IFN-gama and IL-2 is superior to DOX alone.
IFN-gamma, IL-2, or their combination with DOX, are of limited value for the treatment of colorectal cancer in the rat.

the use of IL-2, and IFN gamma, as a single agent in the treatment of cancer is of no value, but the combination of these cytokines, and DOX, is of significant value in enhancing the antitumoral effects of DOX.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combined administration of IL- 2 and IFN-gamma to animals with a transplantable colo-rectal carcinoma resulted in a significant improvement in the efficacy of DOX without any apparent increase in the gross toxicity associated with this drug.
the combination of IFN-γ and IL-2 with doxorubicin (DXR), a commonly used anticancer agent, can significantly increase the efficacy of DXR.

IL-2 and IFN-gamma, when administered together with the chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin, can significantly increase the antitumoral activity of the chemotherapeutic agent without any apparent increase in the gross toxicity.
